routes.question: Can Abs(D9) be certified by a B9-conjugacy quotient and exact rational transportation flows?
premises: D_n is normal in B_n and B_n conjugation preserves the D_n reflection set
reflection length in D_n equals fixed-space codimension
B_n signed-cycle classes in D_n are indexed by (lambda,mu) with even length(mu)
routes.method: derive the exact signed-cycle quotient and cover multiplicities, clear normalized-flow denominators to integral max flow, then verify the serialized rational flow without importing discovery code
routes.next_test: for the stronger all-n conjecture, prove weighted Hall inequalities or construct a compatible closed kernel; the finite D9 endpoint is complete

routes.question: Is any adjacent-rank D9 transportation system infeasible, admitting an exact min-cut/Farkas obstruction?
premises: the B9 orbit quotient and its rational marginals are exact
routes.method: solve every cleared integer max-flow instance and retain a min-cut if its value is deficient
evidence: all nine exact maximum-flow values equal their required integer scales
routes.failure_reason: A strictly feasible exact primal certificate exists for every adjacent-rank layer, so no infeasibility certificate exists for this D9 LP.

routes.question: Can the finite orbit flows be organized into an all-n recurrence D_n to D_{n+1}?
premises: the signed-bipartition quotient and integer transportation formulation are uniform in n
routes.method: test fixed-point embedding and search for weighted-Hall or closed-kernel identities
evidence: the naive append-a-positive-fixed-point proportionality already fails from D8 to D9
routes.failure_reason: The user fixed the release scope to D9 and prohibited further n>9 extension work. The naive fixed-point proportionality failure is retained only as a limitation, not as a release gate.
